title: Gruelling western tour, his swollen legs, and the musicians' fund
summary: Harris says the long jumps swelled his legs and left him crippled after surgery; talk of a musicians' recording fund.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: When you, when you, you didn't get this stroke on a bandstand, did you?

No, I never had no stroke. No, that's right. Well, I'll tell you what it is. We went to California, those jumps were so long, I'll tell you what it is. You see, we had, when we jumped from here, we had to jump from here to Oklahoma City, that's about 400 miles, in other ways to say. Now from Oklahoma City to Abercrackie, New Mexico, that's about 400 miles apart. From Abercrackie, New Mexico to Las Vegas, that's about 400 miles apart, you know? And you see all those little jumpers like that, well, I was kind of half sick then. All my feet swore up, you know, we don't have no rest, no rest. You go to bed, now you get up, boom, you're gone. You're not just like two, three days rest, well, it's been all right. But you got to be jumping down. We jumped from Frisco, I mean from LA, we got to jump four, five hundred miles to Frisco. The easiest one we had was crossing over the Bay to Oklahoma. That's the easiest one we had. Then we had to come back now. Instead of taking the short route, they took a long ride coming back to our past in Texas. And I think that's the long route.
That's when you stopped getting that on the ride?

When I got swole up on the legs, then when I went to the hospital, the doctor said I had to be operated on that way. And the operated on, well, when I come out, I come out walking crippled. I didn't go in that crippled room, but I come out walking crippled. Yeah. Yeah.
You told me, you told me, you told me, Joe, that, um, that caused you to go on the third floor. Remember when we played up there, you told me that?
No, I didn't go on the third floor, you know indeed. I said I had some friends working up there. Friends? Friends, like. No, I've been on the third floor, I never cracked up, man. No.
Well, I mean, the question is this, you don't have to be in that.
No, I wanted to go up there early because I had two friends up there, boys from Bum around the corners here. They're up there, you know, I'll be drinking all that old bad wine, I imagine that.
Yeah, sometimes it affects you after all.

Some people just have to go on the show. I told you, you told me I could go ahead. Yeah. I said, but it done got too close to 9 off time with no session. Then those people had knocked off. I'm glad I didn't go because the boys told me they had, the boys had stopped at 9 o'clock. We didn't stop at 9 o'clock. No. We stopped at 9 o'clock. We stopped at 9 o'clock. Yeah. See, as soon as the band stopped, well they make them go back to bed and go in and they don't go back to bed. And some of them-
This is where? Charity house. A charity.
Well, we have a musician performing fund they have in New York. Yes, I know. Yeah, yeah.
Yeah, record. Yeah, recording funds, you call it.
